assessment.nobel_worthiness: Strong case on distinctiveness of voice and imaginative scale. Blinding (the Orbitor trilogy) and Solenoid build visionary, densely patterned prose in which memory, body and metaphysical speculation form a sustained architecture. The formal ambition and linguistic density place him in a European tradition of large-scale modernist and post-modernist prose, though his work is its own.
assessment.attribution: Citation would rest on the invention of a metaphysical, body-and-memory-centered prose epic in Romanian, with poetry as a secondary strand. Scope is clear and the credit attaches to one writer.
assessment.maturity: A long, consistent career in poetry and prose, with major late-period works that extend rather than repeat the early ones. The case does not depend on a single book.
uncertainties: Assessment relies on public knowledge, not on a fresh reading of the Romanian originals.
Translation quality for very dense, long prose is uncertain.
Poetry and early work are less well known abroad, so corpus coverage is uneven.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: A poetic project of unusual formal and moral ambition. Purgatory and Anteparadise convert dictatorship-era suffering into long poetic sequences, and the landscape-scale interventions extend poetry into collective memorial form. The voice is unmistakable and the intellectual depth is considerable.
assessment.attribution: Citation would concern poetry as collective memory and witness after state violence, in Spanish. Authorship is clear. The large-scale public works are part of the poetic practice but should not be credited as a political gesture in place of literary achievement.
assessment.maturity: Decades of sustained work and several major books, with a deep and consistent line from the early collections to recent ones.
uncertainties: Poetry in translation loses much of its prosody and rhythm, so judgment depends on how reliable the translations are.
The landscape works are ephemeral and public knowledge of them is mostly secondhand.
Weighing visual and installation practice against the written text is difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: A major modernizing force in Arabic poetry. Songs of Mihyar the Damascene and A Time Between Ashes and Roses recast the language through myth, fragmentation and a continuing argument with inherited forms. His critical essays on tradition add intellectual depth.
assessment.attribution: Citation would cover the renewal of Arabic poetic language and form, with the essays as context for the poetry. The credited writer is unambiguous.
assessment.maturity: A career of many decades with lasting influence on later poets. The position is well established, though the late work is less surveyed here.
uncertainties: Arabic poetry is hard to translate, and the assessment depends on mediated access to the sound and register of the originals.
Political and public statements should not be confused with literary merit.
Coverage of his late collections is incomplete.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Grotesque and mythic forms expose the violence of ideology and development. The Four Books and The Explosion Chronicles show formal invention that goes beyond realism, and his own idea of 'mythorealism' is part of the work. The voice is distinct and the sustained satirical imagination is a clear strength.
assessment.attribution: Citation would concern mythic-grotesque fiction as a means of confronting ideological and developmental violence in Chinese. The credit is clear.
assessment.maturity: A long career and a substantial body of novels in which the method develops and varies. The later books are ambitious, though quality across the whole oeuvre may be uneven.
uncertainties: Translation mediates the linguistic achievement, and the evaluation depends on translators.
Some works are known mainly through circulation outside China, so the full corpus is only partly covered.
Distinguishing literary achievement from political significance requires care.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Carpentaria and The Swan Book are large, polyphonic novels that remake the form through Indigenous sovereignty, oral structures and ecological time. The voice and the formal reach are distinctive and the imaginative depth is considerable.
assessment.attribution: Citation would cover an Indigenous Australian narrative tradition renewed in English-language fiction and nonfiction. The credit is clear and the scope is defined.
assessment.maturity: Fewer novels than some candidates, but each is substantial. Durability looks strong, though the oeuvre is narrower in volume and the case rests on a few central books.
uncertainties: The size of the oeuvre is limited compared with others on the list.
The English of the novels draws on oral traditions that I cannot fully assess.
Nonfiction coverage is thin.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Hybrid forms that cross classical scholarship, lyric, narrative and visual design. Autobiography of Red and Nox show striking formal invention and an unmistakable voice, with intellectual depth drawn from classical antiquity.
assessment.attribution: Citation would address genre-crossing poetry and the renewal of classical material in English. The credit is clear, although the boundary between poetry, essay and translation is fluid.
assessment.maturity: Substantial, consistent output over several decades. Some of the work is occasional, and the question is whether the formal inventiveness adds up to a unified body of major achievement.
uncertainties: Much of the oeuvre is experimental and performance-based, so judging sustained quality is difficult.
Translations of classical texts are a separate category from original work.
Unevenness across the whole body of work is possible.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dense, compressed prose that turns obscure lives and art history into narrative inquiry. Small Lives and The Eleven demonstrate a rare, compact style of high linguistic intensity and moral seriousness.
assessment.attribution: Citation would concern concentrated prose that revisits the biography of the unknown and the origins of art, in French. The credit is clear.
assessment.maturity: A small but highly regarded body of work, with consistent quality. The limited size is a concern for scope and sustained significance.
uncertainties: The style depends heavily on the French original and is difficult to translate.
The oeuvre is short and the case rests on a few books.
Readership outside French-speaking literature is limited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Hybrid travel, essay and fiction map Europe through borderlands, memory and intellectual history. Danube and Microcosms show erudition, a flexible prose and a humanist breadth that fit the idea of an oeuvre of lasting cultural significance.
assessment.attribution: Citation would address a literature of Central European cultural memory in the essay-novel form, in Italian. The credit is clear, though the genre mix makes the scope less easy to define.
assessment.maturity: A long career with consistent seriousness. Some of the work is closer to scholarship and essay than to imaginative fiction, so the weight of the purely literary achievement needs judgment.
uncertainties: The balance between scholarly and imaginative writing affects how the case is framed.
Translation coverage of his later work is not fully known to me.
The case may be seen as familiar and well established, which does not itself prove merit.
